data.title: ADDEX THERAPEUTICS TO REPORT  2026 THIRD QUARTER FINANCIAL RESULTS  AND HOST CONFERENCE CALL ON NOVEMBER 25, 2026
data.description:
Geneva, Switzerland, November 20, 2026 - Addex Therapeutics (SIX and Nasdaq: ADXN), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing a portfolio of novel small molecule allosteric modulators for neurological disorders, today announced that it will report its 2026 Third Quarter Financial Results on November 25, 2026. Tim Dyer, CEO, will provide a business update and review of the Addex product pipeline during a teleconference and webcast for investors, analysts and media at 16:00 CET (15:00 GMT / 10:00 EDT / 07:00 PDT) on November 25, 2026.

Title:  Addex Therapeutics Reports 2026 Third Quarter financial results and Provides Corporate Update
Date: November 25, 2026
Time: 16:00 CET (15:00 BST / 10:00 EST / 07:00 PST)

Joining the Conference Call:

  1. Participants are required to register in advance of the conference using the link provided below. Upon registering, each participant will be provided with Participant Dial-in numbers, and a unique Personal PIN.

  2. In the 10 minutes prior to the call start time, participants will need to use the conference access information provided in the e-mail received at the point of registering. Participants may also use the call me feature instead of dialing the nearest dial in number.

Webcast registration link: Registration webcast

Conference call registration link: Registration conference media

About Addex Therapeutics

Addex Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing a portfolio of novel small molecule allosteric modulators for neurological disorders. Addex's lead drug candidate, dipraglurant (mGlu5 negative allosteric modulator or NAM), is under evaluation for future development in brain injury recovery, including post-stroke and traumatic brain injury recovery. Addex has selected a GABAB PAM drug candidate for development in substance use disorders and has successfully completed IND enabling studies. In addition, Addex  is advancing a differentiated GABAB PAM compound for the treatment of chronic cough. Addex holds an 8.5% equity interest in a private spin out company, Neurosterix US Holdings LLC, which is advancing a portfolio of allosteric modulator programs, including M4 PAM for schizophrenia, psychosis and mood-related disorders and mGlu7 NAM for mood disorders. Addex has also invested in Stalicla, a private Swiss company pioneering a precision medicine approach for neurodevelopmental and neuropsychiatric disorders.

Addex shares are listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange and American Depositary Shares representing its shares are listed on the NASDAQ Capital Market, and trade under the ticker symbol “ADXN” on each exchange. For more information, visit www.addextherapeutics.com.

data.title: Asian Equities Tumble as AI Stock Selloff Deepens — Update
data.description:
By Ronnie Harui and Sherry Qin

Asian equities were dragged lower by technology stocks Friday, with Taiwan's benchmark index heading for its worst week in decades as concerns over lofty artificial-intelligence valuations and returns on heavy investment fueled a broader market selloff.

Anthropic's record-breaking initial public offering failed to halt the selling, while gold and silver slid to their lowest levels in more than a year amid expectations of higher interest rates.

"For Asia, the key risk is whether tech equity declines eventually translate into softer hyperscaler capex, semiconductor orders, and physical data-centre investment," said MUFG Bank's senior currency analyst Lloyd Chan.

"That would shift the current tech equity selloffs into a more fundamental growth and export shock," he added.

Taiwan's Taiex sank 6.75%, bringing its weekly loss to more than 17% and putting it on track for its worst week since 1990. Chipmaking giant TSMC fell 5.2%, Foxconn Technology Group dropped 5.4% and MediaTek slumped 9.95%.

The losses came despite tighter restrictions on short-selling introduced Thursday by Taiwan's Financial Supervisory Commission to stabilize the market.

Even strong earnings from Nvidia earlier in the week failed to restore investor confidence, as investors questioned whether heavy AI spending could generate sustainable returns.

Capital Economics warned that the AI boom is becoming increasingly unsustainable, with elevated stock valuations and massive investment plans relying on potentially overoptimistic profit expectations.

CE expects U.S. stocks to fall about 30% from peak to trough by the end of 2027, with a similar decline in Taiwan and a 50% drop in South Korea.

South Korea's Kospi plunged 5.7%, dragged down by SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics, which fell 6.6% and 7.1%, respectively. The Korea Exchange briefly halted trading amid the sharp losses.

Japan's Nikkei Stock Average dropped 4.8%, with SoftBank Group plunging 14.6%, memory-chip maker Kioxia Holdings falling 11.3% and semiconductor-testing equipment maker Advantest losing 10.6%.

The pullback in global markets reflected "concerns about how higher interest rates affect technology valuations," said Antonio Di Giacomo, senior market analyst at XS.com.

The Technology Select Sector SPDR exchange-traded fund, which tracks technology stocks in the S&P 500, entered bear-market territory Thursday, closing more than 20% below its October peak.

Anthropic, the maker of the Claude chatbot, raised about $81 billion in the largest IPO on record. Its shares opened more than 30% above their $83 offering price before paring gains to close 17% higher, giving the company a market capitalization of roughly $1.3 trillion.

"Rather than acting as a rising tide, the listing appeared to trigger rotation out of existing AI-related names as investors redeployed capital into the new issue," Commerzbank Research said.

Government bonds rallied as the equity selloff drove investors toward safer assets.

Australia's two-year government bond yield fell 1.8 basis points to 4.6410%, while New Zealand's two-year yield declined 2.6 basis points to 3.8640%. The two-year U.S. Treasury yield dropped 3 basis points to 4.7300%. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

"Risk aversion intensified, driving demand for U.S. Treasurys," OCBC Group Research strategists said.

data.title: Samsung Electronics Appoints New Memory-Chip Business Head
data.description:
By Kwanwoo Jun

Samsung Electronics has appointed Sang Joon Hwang as head of its memory-chip business, as the South Korean technology giant seeks to strengthen the competitiveness of its semiconductor operations.

Hwang previously led the development of memory-chip products, including dynamic random-access memory and high-bandwidth memory, Samsung said Friday.

The company also named Sangyeun Cho, who previously oversaw its U.S. semiconductor operations, as head of its system large scale integration business.

Vice Chairman and Co-Chief Executive Young Hyun Jun will continue to lead the company's entire semiconductor business, called the Device Solutions division, which comprises its memory, system LSI and foundry businesses, Samsung said.

data.title: LEPAS Officially Enters the Middle East with “Elegance Unbound”
data.description:
DUBAI, United Arab Emirates and WUHU, China, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- LEPAS, Chery Auto’s Premium NEV brand, officially launched in the Middle East with a brand event in Dubai themed “Elegance Unbound” on November 18. The event brought together the LEPAS L8, L6 and L4 for their first joint showcase in the Gulf, with the L8 PHEV set to lead the brand’s market rollout across Middle Eastern markets.


[LEPAS Debuts Its Full Model lineup In The Middle East Market]

“Elegance transcends boundaries while reflecting local cultures. Through design, we connect different aesthetic perspectives; through technology, we bring confidence and peace of mind. We look forward to working with people across the Middle East to make elegance part of everyday life,” said Zhai Xiaobing, CEO of LEPAS.


[ Zhai Xiaobing, CEO of LEPAS]

Building Local Connections Across the Middle East

LEPAS plans to establish lasting customer relationships through localized products, sales and service networks, and lifestyle collaborations. The L8 PHEV has completed 10,000 kilometres of road testing across several Gulf countries, combining a spacious cabin and extended range for daily commutes, intercity travel and longer road trips. The L4 will focus on agile urban mobility, while the L6 will offer intelligent technology and everyday comfort. All three will launch in phases across Gulf markets.


[Scenes From The Middle East Brand Launch Event]

Over the next two years, LEPAS plans six models spanning A–D segments, including plug-in hybrid and hybrid powertrains, with future launches tailored to local market needs and customer lifestyles.


[ LEPAS L8 PHEV]

Working with regional partners, LEPAS will expand its sales and after-sales network, giving customers access to vehicle experiences, purchasing services and ongoing support. A Jebel Ali parts warehouse will serve six Gulf countries, targeting a 48-hour response to spare-parts requests. Partnerships with regional creators and automotive media, participation in platforms including EV WORLD, and customer experiences in shopping and lifestyle destinations will strengthen local engagement.

Making Elegance Unbound a Local Experience

Following launches in Southeast Asia and Europe in 2026, LEPAS’s Middle East entry advances its global expansion. “Elegance Unbound” expresses a balance between consistent global design and quality standards and the cultural identities of individual markets. By listening to local customers and embracing different perspectives, LEPAS aims to create an expression of elegance that feels distinctive to each market while remaining true to its global identity.


[Scenes From The Middle East Brand Launch Event]

About LEPAS

LEPAS is Chery Auto's Premium NEV brand, dedicated to creating elegant mobility experiences for users worldwide. Committed to becoming the Preferred Brand for Elegant Mobility Life, LEPAS brings together Leopard Aesthetics, Elegant Technology, and Exquisite Space - transforming elegance into a driving experience you can see, feel, and trust. Supported by a growing global dealer network of more than 500 sales and service outlets, LEPAS is expanding its international footprint through localized operations, delivering products and experiences tailored to users across global markets.

About Chery Auto

Founded in 1997, Chery Auto is a global automotive manufacturer specializing in vehicle development, intelligent technologies, and new energy solutions. The company operates in more than 130 countries and regions, supported by a strong international network of research, production, and strategic partnerships. Chery Auto has remained China’s No. 1 passenger vehicle exporter among Chinese brands for 23 consecutive years. Guided by its global philosophy of "In somewhere, For somewhere, Be somewhere," Chery Auto is committed to advancing sustainable mobility through continuous innovation and global collaboration.

data.title: TetraMem Scientists Named Among World's Most Influential Researchers in 2026
data.description:
TetraMem Scientists Named Among World's Most Influential Researchers in 2026

Five members of TetraMem Inc.'s founding and technical team have been named to Clarivate's prestigious 2026 Highly Cited Researchers list.

TetraMem is a pioneer in RRAM-based analog in-memory computing (A-IMC). This concentration of recognized researchers underscores the company's strong technical expertise and its commitment to advancing RRAM technology to address critical bottlenecks in AI computing.

The honorees include Dr. Glenn Ning Ge, Co-founder and CEO; Dr. Joshua Yang, Co-founder and Scientific Board Chief Advisor; and Dr. Qiangfei Xia, Co-founder and Chief Process Advisor. This recognition places them among an elite group representing approximately the top 0.1% of researchers worldwide in terms of scientific influence.

This achievement highlights TetraMem's ability to translate fundamental scientific breakthroughs into cutting-edge semiconductor technologies that address the growing performance and energy challenges of AI computing.

TetraMem has advanced its proprietary RRAM-based A-IMC technology into silicon implementations, including its 22 nm AI computing platform and its 12 nm MLX300 chip, whose tape-out the company announced on October 27, 2026. The company's product development roadmap also explores advanced-node and data-center architectures.

"Having five globally recognized Highly Cited Researchers on our team is an extraordinary achievement and a testament to the work taking place at TetraMem to translate groundbreaking research into commercially scalable silicon technologies that can redefine the performance, energy efficiency, and scalability of AI computing," said Dr. Glenn Ning Ge, Co-founder and CEO of TetraMem.

About TetraMem

TetraMem Inc. is a Silicon Valley-based semiconductor company pioneering RRAM-based analog in-memory computing technologies for energy-efficient AI applications. Its innovations span memory devices, integrated circuits, computing architectures, and software, targeting edge AI and Physical AI.

Alibaba Group Holding Limited Notice of January 19, 2027 Application Deadline for Class Action Lawsuit - Contact Lewis Kahn, Esq. at Kahn Swick & Foti, LLC, Before Application Deadline

Kahn Swick & Foti, LLC (“KSF”) and KSF partner, former Attorney General of Louisiana, Charles C. Foti, Jr., notifies investors in Alibaba Group Holding Limited (NYSE: BABA) of a class action securities lawsuit.

CLASS DEFINITION: The lawsuit seeks to recover losses on behalf of investors who purchased or otherwise acquired publicly traded Alibaba securities between May 23, 2024 and November 11, 2026, inclusive (the “Class Period”). This action is pending in the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York.

Follow the link below to get more information and be contacted by a member of our team:

https://www.ksfcounsel.com/cases/nyse-baba/

Alibaba investors should contact KSF Managing Partner Lewis Kahn toll-free at 1-833-538-3615 or via email (lewis.kahn@ksfcounsel.com), or visit https://www.ksfcounsel.com/cases/nyse-baba/ to learn more.

>>>CLICK HERE for more information

CASE DETAILS: According to the Complaint, throughout the Class Period, Defendants made materially false and/or misleading statements, as well as failed to disclose material adverse facts about the Company’s business, operations, and prospects.

Specifically, the lawsuit alleges that Defendants failed to disclose to investors that: (i) Alibaba maintained a business relationship with Alice Huang and, through her, Megaspeed, which is suspected of smuggling certain hardware to China illegally; (ii) Alice Huang is suspected of having served as a Chinese spy, and achieved notoriety after her relationship with Jensen Huang, the former CEO of NVIDIA Corporation, was revealed; (iii) the foregoing materially raised the likelihood of reputational damage to Alibaba, as well as the risk that Alibaba would not be able to purchase certain products subject to export control restrictions by the United States; and (iv) as a result, Defendants’ public statements about Alibaba’s business, operations, and prospects were materially false and/or misleading at all relevant times.

The case is Bihan v. Alibaba Group Holding Limited et al, No. 26-cv-10158.

WHAT TO DO? If you invested in Alibaba and suffered a loss during the relevant time frame, you have until January 19, 2027 to request that the Court appoint you as lead plaintiff; however, your ability to share in any recovery does not require that you serve as a lead plaintiff.

data.title: EMEA Morning Briefing: AI Bust Continues
data.description:
MARKET WRAPS

Watch For:

Eurozone flash consumer confidence indicator, France monthly business survey; no major trading updates expected

Opening Call:

European stock futures were lower, after Asia stocks fell. The yield on U.S. Treasurys fell, the dollar weakened. Gold fell and oil edged higher.

Equities:

European equity futures fell, after stocks on Wall Street closed lower in a volatile session as Anthropic's record-breaking initial public offering failed to staunch the bleeding in artificial-intelligence stocks.

"The deepening correction in tech stocks-which was unrelieved by the record-smashing IPO-is casting some doubt on just how much further the [Federal Reserve] will tighten," BMO's chief economist Douglas Porter said.

"While Fed officials continue to sound quite hawkish, softening equities will tighten financial conditions and could limit the extent of rate hikes."

Forex:

The U.S. dollar weakened and may face risk-off sentiment spurred by Wall Street's slide overnight.

"Risk-off is really the sentiment," Andrew Wells, chief investment officer at SanJac Alpha said. "I think we're seeing that kind of play out with Anthropic's IPO opening," as the initial euphoria cooled down during the trading session, he said.

Weakness in equities, in turn, could have implications for monetary policy.

Bonds:

The yield on U.S. Treasurys were edged lower as the Anthropic IPO failed to sustain risk appetite in Wall Street.

The debut on Nasdaq values the AI company at nearly $1.5 trillion, but it doesn't keep investors from rotating away from risky assets. The resulting demand for Treasurys pressures down yields even as markets price in a cycle of Fed hikes.

"The 10-year [Treasury] yield is still well over 5% and the small move down over the past week is indicative of a flight to safety," said Cardiff's Dean Lyulkin.

Energy:

Oil prices rose slightly amid Middle East tensions. A projectile launched by Yemen's Iranian-backed Houthi rebels struck the tallest tower in Saudi Arabia's capital on Thursday.

"Uncertainty around the sustainability of strong Middle East exports could keep oil prices more elevated for longer than expected," said Citi Research analyst Xiaodan Zhu.

Metals:

Gold prices were lower, with silver falling to their lowest levels in over a year as the precious metals were weighed by growing expectations higher interest rates globally.

Expectations for tighter monetary policy appear to have overshadowed the typical demand for the yellow metal as a safe haven for risk-averse investors.

Elevated Treasury yields and a strong dollar are raising the cost of holding the nonyielding yellow metal, said Critical Metals' Tony Sage.

Minutes from the Federal Reserve's October meeting showed that nearly all policymakers expected further interest rate increases will be needed, while weak gold exchange-traded fund flows in recent weeks have added to the subdued investment backdrop, he said

Copper fell to an eight-month low on a likely technical correction after settling higher in the previous session.

Chinese smelters were facing tight concentrate supply, said Zaye Capital Markets analyst Naeem Aslam.

The metal's price direction will likely depend on whether improving Chinese physical demand can offset softening global economic expectations and tighter financial conditions, he added.

TODAY'S TOP HEADLINES

Anthropic's IPO Is a Win for Venture. Its Success Could Reshape the Industry.

Venture backers finally stand to mint returns on the enormous amounts of capital they poured into Anthropic, cementing the idea that making bigger bets in pursuit of even bigger outcomes can pay off.

Anthropic's initial public offering could create lasting change in venture capital, a sector that has evolved to meet the needs of artificial-intelligence startups. Indeed, the company is slated to generate billions of dollars in returns for venture investors. Shares of the company were priced at $83 Wednesday evening, valuing the company at about $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis.

U.S. Has Floated NATO Membership for Ukraine in Recent Meetings

In closed-door peace talks over the past few months, President Trump's son-in-law and special envoy Jared Kushner has discussed an idea once believed to be dead-on-arrival: NATO membership for Ukraine if it cedes territory to Russia, said people familiar with the matter.

Moscow has fought for years to prevent Ukraine from joining the 32-member North Atlantic Treaty Organization. Trump himself ruled out NATO membership for Ukraine early last year as unacceptable to Russia.

TPG, Corpay to Buy Finance Platform Bill for About $6 Billion

Finance platform Bill Holdings will be acquired in a deal valued at about $6 billion, with TPG set to buy a majority stake and Corpay agreeing to buy a minority interest.

Starboard Value, Bill's largest stockholder, has agreed to vote in favor of the $63.25-a-share deal.

About OET
OET is a leading international tanker company providing seaborne transportation of crude oil and refined products. The Company was incorporated on April 30, 2018 under the laws of the Republic of the Marshall Islands and is listed on Oslo Stock Exchange under the symbol OET and the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol ECO. The sailing fleet consists of ten modern scrubber-fitted Suezmax tankers and eight modern scrubber-fitted VLCC tankers.
